title: What’s behind the Google AI shake-up
excerpt: With Google’s Gemini models seemingly behind, and leaders like Jeff Dean and Demis Hassabis moving to new roles, can Google stil compete in AI? We discuss on The Vergecast.
content_html:
David Pierce

is editor-at-large and Vergecast co-host with over a decade of experience covering consumer tech. Previously, at Protocol, The Wall Street Journal, and Wired.

Some of the biggest names on Google’s AI team got new jobs this week. In some cases, including for legendary Googler Jeff Dean, those jobs are no longer at Google. Given that Google’s models seem to be behind the best of what’s coming out of anthropic and OpenAI, is this a sign of Google in turmoil? Is it about Demis Hassabis wanting something more interesting to work on than virtual assistants? Or is there something else entirely happening here?

On this episode of The Vergecast, Nilay and David start by discussing the leadership shake-up at Google, the state of the AI race, and whether Google is actually set up to succeed here. They also talk about the ways in which Google and Reddit have become existentially dependent on each other, and why that dependence is starting to look like a problem.

After that, we talk about Disney’s plan to put even more stuff in the Disney Plus app, David Ellison’s defense of… David Ellison, the scourge of the “time spent” metric, Brendan Carr’s ongoing assault on free speech, the Spider-Man ads appearing in your BMW, and much more.

In case you missed it this week: We also talked about screen-free wearables, open-weight AI models, E Ink screens, and outrageously huge IMAX screens. And we want to hear all your thoughts about all of it! Call the Vergecast Hotline at 866-VERGE11, send us an email at vergecast@theverge.com, and tell us everything that’s on your mind. And make sure you subscribe so you don’t miss an episode!

content_html_zh:
大卫·皮尔斯

是特约编辑和 Vergecast 联合主持人，在消费技术领域拥有十多年的经验。 此前，曾供职于《Protocol》、《华尔街日报》和《连线》。

谷歌人工智能团队的一些知名人士本周获得了新工作。 在某些情况下，包括传奇的谷歌员工杰夫·迪恩（Jeff Dean），这些工作不再在谷歌了。 鉴于谷歌的模型似乎落后于人类和 OpenAI 的最佳模型，这是谷歌陷入混乱的迹象吗？ 是不是 Demis Hassabis 想要做一些比虚拟助理更有趣的工作？ 还是这里完全发生了其他事情？

在 The Vergecast 的这一集中，Nilay 和 David 首先讨论了 Google 的领导层变动、人工智能竞赛的现状，以及 Google 是否真的准备好在这里取得成功。 他们还讨论了谷歌和 Reddit 是如何变得相互依赖的，以及为什么这种依赖开始看起来像一个问题。
